newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt says tankan may not mean economy worse.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt says tankan may not mean economy worse.

text.p: A worse than expected result in the Bank of Japan's August "tankan" corporate survey does not necessarily mean the nation's economy has worsened, chief government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told reporters on Wednesday.
Kajiyama said that just because the headline number was not as good as expected, "it does not necessarily mean that the economy has worsened".
He said that the tankan data had both good and bad figures in it and it was important to read the data carefully.
Asked if the tankan result would prompt the government to draft a supplementary budget for this fiscal year, Kajiyama said: "One does not simply lead to another."
He added that it was necessary for the government to act calmly.

The tankan's diffusion index for major manufacturers, an important gauge of business sentiment, dropped to minus seven from minus three recorded in the previous survey in May. Forecasts by economists ranged from minus two to plus five.
